ANT|Jalese Gordon.bio:
Jalese Gordon was born on 8th November 2001 and started sailing at the age of nine at the Antigua Yacht Club because sheloved the idea of doing any sport associated with the water. A year later, she began to train competitively with the optimist team where she gained the opportunity to compete both regionally and internationally. She later moved to 4.7 and laser radial where she not only competed but was able to train at the world sailing clinic and secure a position to compete at Youth Worlds. Recently, she gained the opportunity to get the Olympic scholarship and compete in the Summer Olympics in Tokyo in 2021. Moving from competing in dinghy sailing to bigger boats has always been a dream of hers.
She notes that she feels extremely lucky and honored to be a part of the team. "It's so nice to have teammates that you grew up with because everyone has this form of respect for each other and the knowledge and experience we all bring. I’m super excited and cannot wait to compete with so many amazing sailors from around the world!" Jalese's position on the boat is offside trimmer, which is new to her but notes that it has been an amazing challenge.

In 2010, Shannon was victorious with Oracle Team USA winning his first America’s Cup in a Deed of Gift match and in 2013 was onboard for the greatest comeback in sporting history to defend the Auld Mug in San Francisco. ARG|Alejandro Colla.bio: Alejandro Colla is an americas cup and olympic sailor. He competed in the finn class in the 2004 olympics and he was a member of the +39 americas cup team in the 2007 cup in Valencia, Spain. He is a multiple world champion and has competed in the TP52 class for many years.

ARG|Diego Garay.bio: I was born in La Plata, Argentina. I started sailing on my father's boat and later on in Optimist. I began racing in keelboats at a very young age, first in the J24 class and in rating classes. I graduated with a degree in philosophy from university and worked several years as a teacher. However, I have dedicated most of my life to working as a professional sailor and boat captain. Currently, I mainly sail in the TP52, Maxi, and J70 classes.

ARG|Gabriel Marino.bio: I was born on April 5, 1986, in Mar del Plata, Buenos Aires, Argentina. I started sailing in Optimist, Laser, and J24. During that period, I became the J24 South American Games champion in 1987. I participated in thirteen seasons of TP52 between 2007 and 2020 in the Audi Med Cup and the 52 Super Series. Throughout those years, I achieved two first-place finishes in TP52 World Championships in 2009 and 2015. I also secured the top spot in the annual TP52 circuit in 2012, 2015, 2017, and 2019 with the yacht Azurra.

World Championship: Rolex TP52 World Championship Puerto Portals 2019

ARG|German Panei.bio: German Panei is the Argentinian with more experience in the RC44 Class. He has been a trimmer onboard peninsula pretroleum for many years. His knowledge of the class is and has been key to helping the Argentinian team improve, especially helping the team's young sailors.

ARG|Guillermo Parada.bio: Guillermo Parada is one of Argentina’s most experienced sailors. He has sailed in Optimist, Cadet, 470, Lightning, and won several World and Pan American Championships. He also participated as an athlete at the 1988 Olympic Games and was involved in the 2007 America’s Cup. In addition, he was at the helm of the Siemens at the Audi MedCup Circuit and won four times the 52 Super Series as the helm of the Azzurra team.

World Championship: Rolex TP52 World Championship Puerto Portals 2019

ARG|Jordan Rivas.bio: Originally from Rosario, Argentina, I hold a degree in Industrial Chemistry. My passion for sailing has led me to navigate in various classes of vessels, from J24 and Soto33 to GS32, IMS, Maxi, and classic boats. In 2019, I achieved victory in the Maxi World Championship in Sardinia. Likewise, in the Soto40 World Championships in 2012 and 2015, I secured impressive second and third positions, solidifying my reputation in international nautical competitions.

World Championship: Allianz 2022 Youth Sailing World Championships Women
Rolex TP52 World Championship Puerto Portals 2019

ARG|Mariano Parada.bio: Mariano “Cole” Parada holds six World Champion titles for Cadet, Snipe, Maxi and TP52. He participated at the Sydney 2000 Olympic Games sailing in the Tornado Class and was a coach for the Argentina’s Team at Athens 2004. He was part of the Azzurra, one of the most successful 52 Super Series’ teams. Cole was Santiago Lange and Cecilia Carranza’s coach for the Rio 2016 Olympics and was involved in the Victory Challenge team for the 2007 Louis Vuitton Cup.

World Championship: Rolex TP52 World Championship Puerto Portals 2019

ARG|Mateo Majdalani.bio: Mateo Majdalani has evolved from a young sailing promise to a well-known and established sailor. He sailed in Optimist, 420, 29er (in which he obtained two bronze medals at World Championships) and was the helm for the Arg Youth Team at the Red Bull Youth America’s Cup Selection Series in 2013. Santiago Lange and Cecilia Carranza had him as a coach for the Rio 2016 Olympics, where they obtained the Gold Medal. Mateo is currently sailing in Nacra 17 with Eugenia Bosco and won the Silver Medal at the 2019 Pan American Games, and is now aiming for Paris 2024.

ARG|Santiago Lange.bio: Santiago Lange is, without any doubt, one of Argentina’s most famous sailors. He has both an amazing career, and an inspiring personal story. Olympic, World and South American Champion in several classes, he also won the gold at the 2016 Rio Olympic Games in Nacra 17. Last but not least, he has raced with the Artemis Racing team for the 2013 America’s Cup, and the Telefonica’s crew of the 2008 Volvo Ocean Race.

World Championship: Rolex TP52 World Championship Puerto Portals 2019

AUS|Annie Wilmot.bio: Annie Wilmot grew up sailing on Sydney Harbour. She excelled in her youth sailing, winning the 2016 Youth World Championship in the 29er, before progressing into the Olympic class of the 49erFX. Annie is a member of the Australian Sailing Team since 2018. Annie competed in the first ever Womens Americas Cup in 2024, trimming on the port side of the AC40.

AUS|John Bertrand.bio: He is a two time Olympian in the Finn, attaining a Bronze Medal at the Montreal Olympics of 1976. Now often referred to simply as ‘The Great Man’, John Bertrand AO was the Skipper of Australia II when that crew wrestled away the Auld Mug from the New York Yacht Club after 132 years of dominance. Now the Boxing Kangaroo, and to a lesser extent the blue skirt worn by Australia II whenever she was hauled out, remain very much front and centre in the mind of the Captain. No doubt this is because of the scale of that crew’s achievements, but also because of the very nature of the person. Bertrand epitomises both the famous Aussie ‘Can Do’ attitude, and never-failing sense of humour. Time with Bertrand is to be cherished, and there are always absolute pearls of wisdom on offer too. One such example is how faced with enormous gravity at 3:1 down, the Captain implored his crew to remove everything from their minds and just look at one race at a time. And for three more races they did just that! Of course the Antipodeans are also known for owning a decent soupçon of brashness and desire to just get on with it. In olden times it might have been called larrikinism, whereas today it is given the more friendly term of fun loving. The tales of the Australia II crew running through the American squad, as they went about their morning run, are as entertaining as they are insightful. Bertrand is the Chairman of the Sport Australia Hall of Fame, whose members are Australia’s sporting royalty and still very actively involved in his beloved Etchells. He won his first of two World Championships in this highly competitive class in 2010, and then his second in 2016. The former was raced in Ireland with Andrew Palfrey and Tom Slingsby as crew. John has always been keen to help bring athletes on, which is one of the reasons he is still so much involved in sport to this day, but in 2010 after winning the Etchells Worlds with John, Slingsby would then go on to win the World Laser Championships, and also be anointed the World Rolex Sailor of the Year.

AUS|Laura Harding.bio: Grew up sailing minnows in Melbourne then transitioned to 420's in youth sailing. After becoming Vice World Champion in the 420 and Junior World Champion in 2018, shifted into the 49erFX in 2019. Teamed up with Annie Wilmot in 2021 and pursuing Olympic campaigning. Co-helmed the Australian Women's America's Cup in 2024.

AUS|Mark Bulka.bio: From the age of 5 I became hooked on sailing, always looking for a race and another challenge. Sailing a Finn put me on a pathway to perfect the sport. Have now won 4 x World Championships many Australian and International Championships in classes like Finns, Contenders, Etchells, A Class Cat, SB20 and Sydney 38s.

AUS|Paul Mckenzie.bio: Paul Mckenzie born in Victoria Australia in a sailing family. In his first years of sailing, he progressed through junior classes into catamarans. Then, he moved into Olympic sailing with the Finn and Americas Cup. Now he is racing big boats and coaching.

BRA|Alfredo Rovere.bio: With more than 30 years of experience in internationalc and ocean racing, Alfredo Rovere has great ambitions in the first edition of the SSL Gold Cup. Born in Buenos Aires, Argentina, the athlete has lived in Brazil since 2000 and obtained naturalization six years ago. In addition to dedicating himself to sailing, Rovere holds a degree in Business Administration, from IBMEC-RJ, and in Yacht Design, from the Westlawn Institute of Marine Technology, in the United States. The bowman will carry the number 1 on the back of his uniform.

BRA|Joao Signorini.bio: After years of competing in the Laser class, he switched to Finn and became an Olympic sailor at the Athens Games (2004), finishing 10th. He also accumulates participations as a crew member in the Volvo Ocean Race by the teams Brasil 1, Ericsson 4, Telefónica and Team AkzoNobel, and by Team SCA, as a coach. In addition, he coached the Greek Ioannis Mitakis at Rio-2016 and worked alongside the Brazilian Jorge Zarif.

BRA|Kahena Kunze.bio: Like Martine Grael, Kahena Kunze comes from a traditional sailing family. The two-time Olympic champion athlete met her partner when she was still a teenager. The two won the 2009 Youth World Cup. And after a reunion they became two-time Olympic champions, in addition to winning titles and more titles at 49erFX.
BRA|Kahena Kunze.club: Iate Clube do Rio de Janeiro

BRA|Pedro Trouche.bio: Champion of the SSL Finals 2018 alongside Jorge Zarif, Pedro Trouche has been a highlight in the Brazilian sailing scene. In April 2022, he became champion of the Brazilian Finn, held by YCSA - Yacht Club Santo Amaro, with 25 boats in the lane. The athlete from Niterói (RJ) is one of the most sought after sailors in the country in local and international regattas.

BRA|Robert Scheidt.bio: The greatest Olympic medalist in Brazil alongside Torben Grael, with five medals, Robert is an athlete who never tires of proving that he can go further. In the Star class, he collected silver in Beijing (2008) and bronze in London (2012), in addition to three world titles (2007, 2011 and 2012). In the Laser class, he won gold in Atlanta (1996) and Athens (2004), and silver in Sydney (2000), in addition to eleven world titles: 1991 (juvenile), 1995, 1996, 1997, 2000, 2001, 2002, 2004 and 2005 and 2013. At the age of 48, he will compete in Tokyo for his seventh Olympics, a record among Brazilians.

Continental Championship: Semana de Buenos Aires 2025 - J70 Sudamericano

CAN|Ansel Koehn.bio: Ansel hails from the Cowichan Valley on Vancouver Island, BC, and currently serves as the bowman for Team Canada. In this role, he ensures the proper hoisting and lowering of sails. Ansel's limited experience in match racing has cultivated agility and speed, crucial for adapting to sudden plan changes. Recently, he has been fulfilling the mid bow position on a Pac52, enhancing his understanding of the boat's style and maneuver mechanics. With a background in smaller boats, including the 29er, and coaching from the Royal Victoria Yacht Club, Ansel has remained well-versed in windward-leeward style racing through various vessels like the VX1, J70, and Melges 24 across North America.

CAN|Drew Mitchell.bio: Drew Mitchell, a seasoned sailor and coach, initially learned the ropes at the Lunenburg Yacht Club. With over 20 years of experience, Drew has dedicated his expertise to high-performance one-design boats. His sailing journey includes racing lasers until the age of 18 and subsequently coaching high-performance dinghies during university. Post-graduation, he ventured into sailmaking at North Sails Vancouver, focusing on Farr 30s, Melges 24s, Martin 242s, and the Bluenose class for the past 15 years. Drew consistently achieves podium and winning positions in national and North American championships across various one-design classes. Recently returning to Nova Scotia with his wife Brittany, Drew is set to lead North Sails Atlantic in Lunenburg, Nova Scotia. His favorite class is the Bluenose, and he holds Chester Race Week in high regard as his preferred regatta in Canada.

CAN|Jackson Macaulay.bio: Jackson Macaulay, a 20-year-old sailor from Halifax, Canada, boasts a 14-year sailing career. Starting in the Optimist, he attended five IODA events, including the 2018 Worlds. Transitioning through the I420 and 29er classes, he qualified for the ISAF Youth Worlds in Oman in 2021. Exploring the 49er and Nacra, Jackson excelled in the Waszp, currently ranking in the top 20 globally. He secured victories at the Canadian National Championship and the Atlantic Coast Championship, and participated in the Sail GP Inspire Program in Chicago, finishing second. Jackson also interned with the Canadian Sail GP Team shore crew in Taranto and Cadiz. His next venture takes him to Australia for the Waszp World Championship. With aspirations of becoming a professional foiling sailor involved with SailGP and the Americas Cup, Jackson Macaulay is a rising force in the sailing world.

CAN|Robert Hemming.bio: Former national champion Canadian sailing team memeber in the Finn class, Rob also has won multiple keelboat titles including 8m world championships. Rob also served as Team Leader at Tokyo 2020 and previous Panam games. Rob is stepping in as Captian for the legendary Richard Clarke, with the goal of further gorwing and developing young talented sailors for Canada.

CHI|Andrés Ducasse.bio: Accurate and methodical. This is our grinder. This position requires strength and sensitivity to know when and how much power to put into the trim of the sails. With his capacity for analysis and observation, Andrés shines in this position. He started sailing Optimist at age 6, and at 10 he made his competition debut. Since then, he has had great successes, being 3 times national champion in different classes, J70 World Champion in the Corinthian category in 2021 and an excellent participation in the Rio 2016 Olympic Games. He is currently a helmsman at J70 and S40.

CHI|Felipe Robles.bio: Dynamic and restless, our helmsman started sailing in Dinghy boats, with great results. He began in the J-24 class as helmsman and tactician in different prominent teams, obtaining Pan American Odesur medals and outstanding participation in world championships. He has great technical dialogue and full confidence in the capabilities of his team.

CHI|Nicholas Robertson.bio: Vigilant and proactive. Our Pitman does not miss one. Because of his experience on different ships and positions, he is the ideal navigator for the Pitman position, as he is located in the nerve center of the ship. All the maneuvers pass through here (hoisting, lowering, giving the correct tension to each halyard according to the intensity of the wind, in addition to the rough ones). He has been sailing in Optimist since he was 8 years old, participating in South American, North American and World Championships. He continued to compete in 420, Snipe, Lightning, J24, J105, Soto40, Oceanicos (ORC, IRC) and J70, where he obtained podium finishes in several national, world, and South American championships. He also has experience in offshore regattas (Fasnet, Caribean 600 and Transatlantic Race). He is currently dedicated to sailing, mainly on J70, Lightning, Soto40 and J105. He is passionate and enjoys sailing (and life in general).

CHI|Rodrigo Robles.bio: Friendly and relaxed on land, focused and competitive in the water. Our Headsail trimmer carries his sails very safely. He is in charge of the trim of the jib (upwind) and the spinnaker (downwind). He is part of the speed team of the boat, and is in charge of permanently adjusting all its controls, depending on the wind and wave conditions. He started sailing Optimist at the age of 8. He went on to sail J70, J24, Laser and S40, where he has been a strong performer, winning national championships in several of these categories. During the breaks between regattas, Rocco is the entertainment of the team, with his dances and his friendliness at all costs.

COL|Ana Sofia Bermudez.bio: Ana Sofia Bermudez is a Colombian sailor dedicated mainly to the sunfish class, where some of her notable results have been: two-time silver medalist at the 2022 and 2023 Central American Games, national women's sunfish champion, 3rd place in the 2022 junior world championship, and 4th place in the 2022 women's world championship. She also has experience sailing 420 and lightning. She compete 3 years in optimist, consistently ranking in the top 3 nationally.

COL|Andrey Quintero.bio:
Olympic athlete in the ILCA class and sailing coach
Andrey Quintero has over 20 years of experience in high-performance sailing, establishing himself as a leading figure in the ILCA class (formerly Laser). He has proudly represented his country at the Olympic Games in the ILCA class, and has competed in 15 ILCA World Championships and five Pan American Games.
Among his most notable achievements is earning the title of World Sailing Vice Champion, a testament to his technical excellence and competitive consistency. In addition to dinghy sailing, Andrey has extensive offshore racing experience as a helmsman and tactician on yachts from 38 to 44 feet, providing leadership and strategic insight at sea.
He is currently active both as a competitive sailor and coach, dedicated to developing the next generation of top-level sailors.

COL|Esteban Echavarria.bio: Esteban Echavarria is a competitive Snipe and Sunfish sailor from Colombia and a two-time Colombian Olympic Committee Athlete of the Year in Sailing. A Bolivarian Games champion in both classes and fourth-place finisher at the Toronto Pan American Games, he has represented Colombia on the international stage for over a decade. He began his career in the Optimist and Laser 4.7, winning events like the U.S. Midwinters and Buenos Aires Sailing Week.

COL|Juan Camilo Bustos.bio: With over 30 years of experience in sailing, Juan Camilo Bustos has built a solid athletic career, competing in classes such as Sunfish, Lightning, and J24. He has achieved outstanding results and podium finishes in national championships, as well as in international events including World, South American, Pan American, Central American, North American, and Midwinters championships. His career has been recognized on multiple occasions for his exceptional performance.

COL|Juan Diego Chaves.bio: 21 years old, currently studying to be a Mechanical Engineer; Juan Diego has been sailing competitively in Colombia since he was 9 years old. He has achieved massive experience in the Optimist, ILCA and Lightning classes; participating in ILCA7 South Americans, CAC games, CAC beach games and Junior South Americans. In the Lightning class, he has participated in Junior North Americans, South Americans and Junior Worlds. However, he has proven to be a highly versatile sailor, competing and excelling in Snipe and Catalina Capri 22 national championships. He specializes in ILCA7, where he has been ranked top 3 for three years in a row, winning silver in 2023 National Games and bronce in 2024 Junior National Games.

COL|Juan Esteban Restrepo.bio:
Juan Esteban Restrepo Vera
Colombian sailor with 18 years of experience, specializing in the Snipe, Sunfish, and ILCA classes. Notable achievements include a gold medal at the 2017 Bolivarian Games, multiple medals at the National Games, several National championship titles, and a fourth-place finish at the 2015 Pan American Games. Twice named Colombia’s Best Sailing Athlete (Altius Award, 2015 and 2017).

COL|Julian Ramirez.bio: Julian Ramirez Arango is a Colombian sailor with 20 years of experience, specializing in the Lightning, Snipe, and Sunfish classes. He began his career in Optimist, later competing in Sunfish and ILCA, where he earned the title of Sunfish Youth World Champion. Representing Colombia in multiple international events—including the Pan American Games and Bolivarian Games—he achieved notable success, such as a third-place finish at the Lightning South American Championship.

COL|Pablo Bright.bio: Pablo Bright began his sailing career at the age of 12 racing Optimist. He's been racing Lightnings since 2015, participating in numerous national events and racing internationally at the 2021 Youth North American Championship and 2023 World Championship and South American Championship. He's also an avid ILCA sailor, with podiums at national level and taking part in the 2023 South American Championship. He has raced in Snipe, 420 and Sunfish at national level, and Sunfish in the 2018 South American Championship. In 2024 he won the 'Copa Cruceros Tominé' crewing a Capri 22.

COL|Samuel Hormiga.bio: Samuel Hormiga began his sailing career in 2003 in the Sunfish class, achieving a top 10 national ranking. Since 2010, he has worked as a coach in the Optimist, Sunfish, and ILCA classes. He is a physical trainer specialized in sailors and is currently pursuing a Master's degree in Sports Science, focusing on the preparation of high-performance athletes. He is currently the coach of the Santander Sailing Team and served as a coach for the Colombian National Sailing Team at the 2023 Pan American Games held in Santiago, Chile.

CUB|Darien Martinez Pimentel.bio: Darién Martínez Pimentel was born on (9/2/1979) with a degree in physical culture and a specialist in sports and recreational sailing. As an athlete, he won a silver medal in the Central American and Caribbean Games (Cartagena 2006), 7th place in the Pan American Games (Rio 2007), national champion in the Cadet classes (1994), Laser II (1996 and 1997), 470 (2002 ) ) and Snipe (2008). As a coach in the Snipe class, he won Silver and Bronze medals at the Central American and Caribbean Games (Veracruz 2014 and Barranquilla 2018), 7th and 4th at the Pan American Games (Toronto 2015 and Lima 2019), won the Zimmerman and Dudley Gamblin Memorial trophy ( winter circuit Snipe 2017), Bronze Medal in the Pre-Pan Americans (Lima 2018), 8th Place in the Western Hemisphere Championship (Buenos Aires 2018), national champion from 2009 until the activity.

Central American and Caribbean Games Barranquilla 2018. Pan American Games Lima 2019. South American Laser Paracas Peru 2018. North American Laser Vancouver Canada 2017. He is a 4-time national champion in the Laser class and multi-medalist in the optimis class. He has a degree in Physical Culture and Sports.
