CZE|Martin Trcka.bio: Formal laser sailor who participated on Olympic Games in Athens 2004 and Beijing 2008. Martin has huge experience sailing big boats, as he took part on regattas such as Sidney - Hobart or Tour de France a la Voile. He is currently sailing Melges 24 and other big boats.

CZE|Petr Fiala.bio: He has been sailing since the age of six when he achieved many successes on both the national and international regattas. In SSL Petr can leverage his experience of sailing as helmsman on different classes ranging from small dinghies to big boats while finishing many times on podium at Worlds and European championships.

CZE|Sara Tkadlecova.bio: Sara started sailing at age of 6, as a crew on Cadet. As junior, she sailed 29er for 2 years, both helming and crewing. At age of 17 she started the Olympic campaign towards the Olympic Games in Tokyo 2020 on 49erFX with Dominika Vaďurova, in the end they missed the qualification spot by a whisker. Nowadays, she is still sailing 49erFX fulltime, towards Olympic Games in Paris 2024.

CZE|Tomas Vika.bio: Started sailing at age of 6. Single-handed journey took from Optimist through Europe, to Finn class. Multiple National Champion, Vice European Junior Champion, ran Olympic campaign for London 2012 and Rio 2016 Olympic games. In multi-handed classes mostly sailed Melges 24 (European Sportsboat Champion) and one design regattas (Vice World Universities Champion) as a skipper, tactician and main sail trimmer. Loves physical demanding sport activities like XTERRA and half Ironman distances triathlon

CZE|Vojtech Lambl.bio: He has been sailing since the age of six when he achieved many successes on both the national and international regattas. In SSL Petr can leverage his experience of sailing as helmsman on different classes ranging from small dinghies to big boats while finishing many times on podium at Worlds and European championships. Start sailing at age 7 on Optimist but after just a few regattas switched to Cadet class on which he raced on several European championships. After this episode he started to sail on Fireball class which he sails till present time. During this time he also tried plenty other classes like Melges 24, Devoti 1, 29er, 420 and others whit few acchievments on national level. At the age of 18 he started his coaching career and was part of the team which re-started training program in one sailing club. He trained many sailors on Optimist which than achieved several good results in their careers. He also trained handicapped people and adults with no sailing experience. Many of them than started to race. He is also involved in Czech sailing association as a member of the board and is chairman of one of the most successful sailing clubs in Czech Republic.

ECU|Alfredo Ochoa.bio: Sailing since he was 5 years old, Alfredo has been an active sailor for more than 25 years. He started as an Optimist sailor, competing at several Southamerican and World Championships. He also won the National Championship in Opti Team Racing. He has also sailed Lasers, 470, Sunfish, ORC and Lightning Class, where he has obtained three podium positions at the Lightning Class Southamerican Championship, and obtained the Southamerican Championship in 2019 with Julio Velez and Irene Suarez. Alfredo is currently sailing Lightning Class and ORC racing on board a Swan 45, performing as mainsail trimmer/tactician and occasional skippering.

ECU|Alisson Haon.bio: Started sailing in 2023 as crew for the Ecuadorean Team for Panamerican Games. She got 5th at Panam Games, Then she won the southamerican champioship in the Lightning Class and one week later, she won the Worlds Champioship in Lightning Class. Since then she has establish her self as an excelent crew part of the ecuadorean team

ECU|Irene Suarez.bio: Irene better known as "Bebe" for being the youngest of the group. However, at his young age she has achieved many national and international achievements. Being multiple national champion and at the time South American champion of the lightning class. She has managed to receive the award for best female sailing athlete from the Ecuadorian Olympic Committee for more than 4 consecutive occasions.

Continental Championship: II Copa Federacion Peruana de Vela

ECU|John Birkett.bio: John started in the Optimist class in Salinas, where he has lived all his life and is the city where sailing is most practiced in Ecuador. He has more than 15 years of sailing and continued his career representing his country in several classes including 470, Laser, Lightning, Snipe and Sunfish, obtaining international titles at the junior and senior level. He has been national champion on multiple occasions and in different classes. A passionate sailor with a strong character who always seeks to give his best in the water.

Continental Championship: II Copa Federacion Peruana de Vela

ECU|John Wiener.bio: Started saling at 7 in Salinas zacht club Ecuador passioned about saling current Orc chambion an 2nd in National Lightning Championship

ECU|Jonathan Martinetti.bio: Since he was 11 years old, he was a sailor starting in the Optimist class, achieving many national and international titles. He has been South American Optimist Champion, two times Sunfish World Champion, three times Junior World Champion in three different classes, Pan American Champion in Sunfish class in Toronto 2015, and some other awards in the South American Olympic Circuit. He is passionate about sailing, competition, and the sea.

ECU|Juan Andres Santos.bio: Sailing Lightning since he was 10 years old as crew. Have sailed important championships as North Americans, World Championships, and South Americans representing Ecuador. He won a South American championship as a crew and has been second and third various times. He has represented the country in the Pan-American Games on three different occasions.

Continental Championship: II Copa Federacion Peruana de Vela

ECU|Julio Velez.bio: More than 30 years sailing, achieving many titles nationally and internationally. He has represented his country on many occasions in events both on the South American Olympic Circuit and in the region, achieving outstanding performances including the title of South American Champion of the Lightning Class. He is currently the helmsman of the lightning team and crew of a Swan45 acting as the team's tactician.

Continental Championship: II Copa Federacion Peruana de Vela

ECU|Samuel Herrera.bio: He started sailing at the age of 10 in the optimist class, then in the laser radial, sunfish, and lightning. In all these boats, he participated in numerous South-American and world championships. He has raced as a crew member in the lightning class for most of his sailing career. He started racing in the ORC class, and since then, he has raced between this class and lightning.

ECU|Sebastian Herrera.bio: He started in the optimist class when he was nine years old; since then, he has sailed in the laser, sunfish, lightning, and ORC classes. As a crew attended 2 Pan American Games in the lightning class and several South Americans and world championships. In the present day, he races as a skipper in the lightning class and in the ORC class as a crew member.

ESP|Alejandro Muscat.bio: Alejandro Muscat had been a member of the Spanish Olympic team in Laser and Finn from 2005 to 2021. Additionally, throughout his career, he has combined his involvement with cruising and match racing.

ESP|Javier De la Plaza.bio: He won a gold medal at the 2000 49er World Championships and two medals at the 49er European Championships, silver in 1999 and bronze in 2001. He participated in the 2000 Sydney Olympics, placing fourth in the 49er class (along with Santiago López-Vázquez). He currently sails in cruising, TP52, RC44 and ClubSwan

World Championship: Rolex TP52 World Championship PORTO CERVO 2026
Rolex TP52 World Championship Puerto Portals 2019

ESP|Pedro Mas.bio: Professional sailor since the age of 18, previous training in Optimist, 420 and 470. Currently sailing in Tp52, Maxis and Swan50.

World Championship: Rolex TP52 World Championship Puerto Portals 2019

EST|Ago Rebane.bio:
Ago has been sailing for over 45 years. In the past decade, he has been crowned as the World Champion 
in the X-41 class in 2010 and in the Platu25 class in 2021. In addition, Ago has two silver medals from 
European Championships in match racing. All these results have been achieved in Mati Sepp’s team. In 
SSL Team Estonia, Ago’s position is the mainsail trimmer.

EST|Janno Hool.bio:
Janno is a former Finn sailor who now collects medals in Mati Sepp’s team. His recent achievements 
include a gold medal at the Platu 25 World Championships in 2021, a bronze medal at the Platu25 World 
Championships in 2019. At European Championships in match racing in 2016 and 2018, Janno was 
awarded with a silver medal.

EST|Karl Kolk.bio:
Karl is a versatile bowman who is well-known in match racing, one design (X-99, X-35, X-41 and Platu 25)
and ORC racing. Being part of Mati Sepp’s match racing team, they have managed to maintain a TOP10
position in the match racing ranking throughout several years. Karl has also been crowned as the World
Champion in the X-99 and the Platu 25 class and been victorious at the legendary Copa del Rey.
Definitely a dream bowman for every boat!

EST|Karl-Hannes Tagu.bio:
In the past, Karl-Hannes spent a lot of time sailing on the ice in the winter, first with the Ice Optimist and later in the most popular DN iceboat class. A real icebreaker! As his father was a sailor and boat builder,
Karl-Hannes has also been involved in the technical development of offshore and keelboats since he was a child. Today, he is a 3-time European champion in offshore sailing.
He also often drives match races."

EST|Mati Sepp.bio:
Mati is the dream tactician for every team. He is always among the top sailors in the ranking of world 
match racing, which makes him one of the best European match race sailors. Mati has the title of World 
Champion in the X-41 and the Platu 25 class, two silver medals from the European Championships match 
race and several other championship titles and medals in the X-99, X-35, Platu 25 and ORC classes.

EST|Peter Saraskin.bio:
Peter has participated in two Olympic Games in the Laser class and came 7th at the World
Championships. He also has extensive experience in the X-99 class as the holder of two silver medals and
one bronze medal at the World Championships. Peter is definitely one of the most skilled trimmers on
large yachts in Estonia, which makes him an invaluable asset for the team.

EST|Taavi Valter Taveter.bio: Taavi Valter is a talented Finn sailor whose best achievement so far is the silver medal at the U23 World Championships in 2020. His favourite hobby is strength training, which makes him a very powerful grinder for SSL Team Estonia. Jumping quickly in and out of water is also not a problem for Taavi Valter, which makes him extremely valuable in case of any seaweed trouble!

FRA|Ange Delerce.bio: Ange Delerce is one of the youngest sailor in the team representing the New Generation. Ange started in the Optimist but it is in the 420 that he displays very promising results. A Silver medal at the 2021 Worlds in Italy followed by a European title and top place at the French Junior Match Racing championship in 2022 bring him within the top ten of France global rankings. These results allowed him to be selected in Team France to participate in the Gold Cup where he will take the position of floater. His role is to help anyone in the team who has a problem, he helps to bring great fluidity to the crew. For this, he adapts easily to any situation and has great mobility on the boat.

World Championship: The 2024 Youth Match Racing World Championships

FRA|EMERIC MICHEL.bio: Emeric Michel is the Captain choice #3 and joined the Team in April 2021. During the first trainings in Switzerland, Emeric displayed his skills as performer, concentrating on the boat speed. The 31 years old engineer mainly sails on inshore keelboats like the SB20, J70, TP52 and on the Match racing circuit.

FRA|Eliott MICHAL.bio: Eliott Michal, hailing from the idyllic French island in the Indian Ocean, Réunion, began his sailing journey in 2002 with the Optimist class, a passion he pursued until 2010. At the age of 16, he embarked on a new adventure in France, honing his skills in the L20 class until 2015. Starting in 2016 and continuing until 2022, Eliott navigated the waters of Marseille as part of the L70 class. Alongside his Olympic aspirations, he initiated a professional sailor career, captaining boats ranging from 30 to 70 feet in racing competitions, now serving as his primary focus.

World Championship: The 2024 Youth Match Racing World Championships

FRA|Loïck Peyron.bio: Loïck Peyron, born 1 December 1959 in Nantes, is a French yachtsman, younger brother of the yachtsman Bruno Peyron. He is particularly famous for winning many races in the 1990s on board his trimaran Fujicolor. Among his notable achievements, he won the ORMA Championship four times in 1996, 1997, 1999 and 2002, the STAR transatlatic race three times, the transat Jacques Vabre twice and won the Jules Verne Trophy in 2012. After Benjamin de Rothschild gave him control of the Gitana Team in April 2006, the team built Gitana Eighty, a 60 feet monohull, launched in July 2007 with which Loick Peyron won the Transat. On 9 December 2008, he began his participation in the 2008-2009 Vendée Globe with Gitana Eighty. After having led the race for 16 days, Gitana Eighty's mast broke. In 2010, Peyron sailed in the 33rd America's Cup as part of the Alinghi Team, in the roles of 'floater' in race 1 and relief helmsman in race 2. Alinghi were defeated by the American challenger BMW Oracle Racing. In early 2012 he won the Jules Verne Trophy in a time of 45 days 13 hours 42 minutes 53 seconds, breaking Franck Cammas previous record by 2 days. In late 2012 he was asked to join Artemis Racing, Challenger of Record for the 34th America's Cup, as one of the helmsmen. He brings a great amount of knowledge and expertise of multihulls to the campaign. In November 2014, he won the Route du Rhum single-handed transat on Banque Populaire VII maxi trimaran. He set the new record, travelling from Brittany to Guadeloupe in 7 days 15 hours 8 minutes and 32 seconds (22.93 kts average speed) and beating Lionel Lemonchois 2006 record by 2h 10mn 34s. In May 2016, he entered the Single-Handed Trans-Atlantic Race aboard Pen Duick II, the boat sailed by Éric Tabarly to win this very race in 1964.

FRA|TIMOTHEE ROSSI.bio: After a classic career in optimist and very good results in 420, Timothée is now the skipper of a project in match race and J70. He now aims to follow the path of the great champions present on the SSL France team.

World Championship: 2022 Youth Match Racing World Championship - Pornichet (J80)

FRA|Xavier Rohart.bio: Xavier Rohart has left his print on french sailing after 6 Olympic Campaigns in Finn and Star. His achievements include a Bronze medal at the Athens Olympic Games and 4 World titles in the Star and J80. Xavier is also the SSL Team France manager, discovering talents in the rich diversity and potential of french sailors

GBR|Aaron Cooper.bio: Grown up dingy sailing south coast of the UK, Aaron quickly moved into keelboat sailing in the Costa del Solent. Progressing to a racing the Figaro 2 in France and then with Dongfeng Volvo Ocean Race Team. Now racing in the 44Cup with Chris Bake´s highly successful Team Aqua.

GBR|Ian Williams.bio: The 43-year-old captain of SSL Team GBR is the most successful skipper on the international match racing circuit. The former lawyer turned professional sailor was the first British skipper to win the Match Racing World Championship and has gone on to make history winning the prestigious title a further five times. Recently he has proved he has lost none of his competitive edge winning two of the world’s leading match racing events, the Congressional Cup and Argo Group Gold Cup in 2019.

World Championship: Shenzhen Baoan Match Cup / WMRT Final 2025
World Championship - Shenzhen Baoan Match Cup 2024
WMRT Final & World Championships - Shenzhen Baoan Cup

GBR|James Dodd.bio: I started sailing at the age of 7 at Keyhaven, a town near Lymington. I progressed through the Britsh youth sailing program in Cadets and 420s representing GBR at World and European championiships After dinghys i moved into keelboats and also trained as a boat builder constructing exocet international moths. in my keelboat career so far i have been fortunate enough to have raced on the RC44 and TP52 classes as well as being a member of Team AkzoNobel in the 2018 Volvo Ocean Race and Currently a member of Team Argo´s MOD 70. I am a big Arsenal fan!

GBR|Matt Cornwell.bio: Coming from the UK’s sailing hotspot of Lymington, Matt Cornwell is one of the UK’s most sought-after bowmen. Having cut his teeth with the GBR Challenge America’s Cup campaign in Auckland in 2003, Cornwell was with the French Areva Challenge in Valencia four years later before joining Team Origin and ultimately the INEOS Team UK America's Cup challenge.

World Championship: Shenzhen Baoan Match Cup / WMRT Final 2025

GBR|Nic Asher.bio: Nic began sailing aged four on the Norfolk Broads. He followed the Royal Yachting Associations Youth system, winning multiple National and International titles including a Silver Medal at the 420 World Championships in 2002. In 2004 Nic was selected into the World Class Performance program in the 470 Olympic Class with his team mate Elliot Willis. They quickly rose to the top, winning the 470 World Championships in 2006. Unfortunately, due to an injury to Elliot in 2007, they missed out on selection for the Beijing Olympic Games. The pair came back stronger in 2008 winning the World Championship for a seond time and the European Championships. Unfortunately they did not have the opportunity to add the Olympic title as well. After medalling at every regatta in 2010, Nic suffered a health setback and had to step away from sailing to recover. In 2014 Nic hung up his Olympic sailing boots and joined the successful Ran Racing TP52 Sailing Team. Since then Nic has become one of the top Tacticians in the World and currently sails on the TP52 and RC44 circuits.

GBR|Pete Cumming.bio: I started sailing age 8 with my parents, progressed into GBR Team age 15 representing GB at the Cadet Wold championships. Won various national & european titles iin various dinghy and small keelboat classes. Moved Worked for North Sails UK as a sail maker and was my introduction into big boats. Winning Mumm30 national & european chapionships and bronze at the world championships. Moved into Exteme 40´s representing Oman Sail, winning the series in 2009. Also racing with Alinghi in the GC32. After this moving into offshore racing, breaking over 14 world speed records on MOD7'´s & 100 footer Scallywag & Comanche. Current holder of RORC Transatlantic monohull & multihull class. Also record for the fastest crossing of the transpacific.

GBR|Phil Clapp.bio: My sporting career started as a Junior level rower where I represented Great britain at junior world championship Level. I then transitioned to sailing aged 25, I have won the maxi 72 world championships twice and sailed in the 52 super series. I alos hold the current 500m indoor rowing world record of 1:10.5 alongside 4x consecutive world championship titles.

GER|Erik Heil.bio: How to win two 49er World Championship medals within two months and almost dethrone the Olympic Champion, America’s Cup Defender and SSL Ranking’s leader Peter Burling? 49er helmsman Erik Heil (30) from Berlin can tell you all about it. The 2016 Olympic Bronze medalist, together with his crew Thomas Plößel is going to help propel Team Germany to success.

GER|Frithjof Kleen.bio: Frithjof “Frida” Kleen discovered his love for the sport on Berlin’s famous Wannsee. He came sixth at the 2012 Olympics and collected a golden star for winning the 2014 Star World Championships. A European Champion in the Dragon and a World Champion in the Swan 45, Kleen’s strengths include an exemplary fighting spirit, motivational talent and a famous sense of humor. Someone once said “Frida” moves on a boat like an elf with the power of a heavyweight boxer. He will use all of his superpower to push Team Germany in the SSL Gold Cup.

GER|Linov Scheel.bio: The 26-year-old 49er crew member from Kiel is part of the next generation of German skiff talents. Linov Scheel was second at the U23 World Championship in 2018 and finished ninth in the senior field of the Kiel Week in 2020.

GER|Magnus Simon.bio: Conventional training in youth boat classes, followed by a switch to the Laser. Pursued a degree in shipbuilding and is now a sail designer at NorthSails. Sailed various keelboats, such as Melges32, Swan50, and J70.

GER|Markus Wieser.bio: A former number one in the world of Match Racing, Markus Wieser (55) is one of the most successful German sailing pros. As helmsman and world class tactician he holds World Cup titles in many different classes from big boats to Dragon, from 5.5mR to Tempest. Because of his outstanding achievements, Wieser is a popular ambassador for well-known global corporations.

World Championship: Rolex TP52 World Championship PORTO CERVO 2026

GER|Matti Paschen.bio: The successful architect from Hamburg brings a huge amount of big-boat experience and a lot of overview to the team. The 50-year-old trimmer was part of the first German America's Cup campaign and won many titles as a core crew member with Markus Wieser, including numerous international titles.

Continental and Regional Games: Henry Rasmussen Memorial Cup - Danish Championship

GER|Paul Kohlhoff.bio: Germany's most successful Olympic catamaran helmsman brings his bronze medal from Japan to the team. The 27-year-old from Kiel knows how to make boats fast and is a leading figure in the young German foiling generation. With his crewmate Alica Stuhlemmer, Paul Kohlhoff sets course for his third Olympic participation in 2024.

World Championship: 2019 Hempel Youth Sailing World Championships - 29er Girls

GRE|Afrodite Zegers.bio:
Afrodite Zegers-de Kleine – Autobiographical Summary
I was born on 2 December 1991 in Athens, Greece, and moved to the Netherlands at the age of 19 due to family reasons. I hold both Greek and Dutch nationality, speak four languages, and live a life combining professional sport, law, music, and coaching.
I am married to Rogier de Kleine, and we have two dogs, Senna and Charlie.
I hold a Bachelor’s degree in Law from the University of Amsterdam (UvA) and a Master’s in Criminal Law with a specialization in Economic Criminal Law from the Open Universiteit. I currently work as a Change Manager in Financial Economic Crime – Transaction Monitoring at Rabobank in Utrecht.
I am a certified Master Practitioner in Neuro-Linguistic Programming (NLP), applying communication and mindset coaching in both sport and professional settings.
Alongside my legal and coaching work, I am an active classical pianist, having graduated from the Athens Conservatory at the age of 16, and I serve as Head Coach of the Optimist class at the DRCS Yacht Club in Switzerland.
I have held the No. 1 world ranking (World Sailing) in the 470 class from 2017 to 2018, and have won national titles in both Greece and the Netherlands.
Sailing Career Highlights
I began sailing at the age of 9, and have represented both the Netherlands and Greece in top-level international competitions, including two Olympic Games:

GRE|Chrysa Marinou.bio: From a young age, I was drawn to the sea. My father windsurfed, so I naturally tried to follow in his footsteps. I quickly transitioned to dinghies, starting with Optimists and then moving on to 420s. Nowadays, I train adults, form teams, and race together in Platus—an experience that has deepened my understanding of sailing theory and physics, and taught me how to effectively pass that knowledge on to others.

GRE|STYLIANOS NOUTSOS.bio: Born in Athens in 1982. Graduated the University of Correlco in Computer Science. Started sailing at 12 years old in the Optimist class, and then moved on to 420, 470, 29er and finally in 49er. Multi-National champion is the Star class and top podium places in offshore races across Europe in the last 20 years.

HUN|Aron Nemeth.bio: After sailing in different Olympic classes and fuelled by his passion for the seas and oceans, Aron decided to move to Australia in 2003. He has since participated in major big boat events in the FARR40 and SYDNEY38 classes and worked on MAXIs and MINI MAXIs. Due to his international experience in these classes, he has the most knowledge in the team of boats like SSL47.

HUN|Marcell Goszleth.bio: Started sailing on their family classic boat. After sailing in Pirat class, he switched for 470, in which he participated at the Sydney Olympics. Besides other dinghy classes, he sailed different keelboats including Offshore regattas on maxis. Had been coaching in 420 and 29er classes now working as a sailmaker in his own business. Best result is WC 3rd and 2nd at the Europeans.

HUN|Szabolcs Majthenyi.bio: Since his childhood, Szabolcs has raced in different classes, including Optimist, Cadet, and 470. However, since 1992 his full focus has been on his beloved “Flying Dutchman”, where he won 13 world and 5 European championships. Since 1997, he has also worked as a coach and he is currently the head coach of the Hungarian 470 Olympic team, preparing for Tokyo

Continental Championship: 2024 International Flying Dutchman Class European Championship
World Championship: 2025 International Flying Dutchman Class World Championship
2022 International Flying Dutchman class World Championship

HUN|Zsombor Berecz.bio: Without any dispute, the captain is the best active sailor in Hungary, proven by his national (28 national championships won) and international results in both Laser and Finn classes, recognised also by its 22nd SSL ranking. Silver medalist on Tokyo Olympic games and the survival of his beloved Finn as an Olympic class, the SSL Gold Cup is his first venture as team leader in big boats against the world’s best sailors.

HUN|Zsombor Gyapjas.bio: Sailing has been the activity I have been most involved in since I was a child. In 2009 I won my first Hungarian Championship title in Optimist, and since then I have been living my life as a sportsman. For years my brother and I sailed in the top of the 470 Olympic class. In the U23 age group, we managed to achieve a 3rd place in the World Championship, in addition to several international podium finishes. I am currently working as a coach and competitor.

ITA|Alberto Bolzan.bio: Alberto Bolzan is nine-time world champion in one-design classes Melges24, Melges32, Soto40, and Maxi. Furthermore,he did two participations in the Volvo Ocean Race.

ITA|Andrea Totis.bio: Andrea Totis, born in 1998, is the European Junior Champion in 470 and the Junior Vice World Champion in 470. His sailing excellence and consistent performance position him as a rising star in the world of junior sailing.

ITA|Emanuele Marino.bio: Emanuele Marino, I participated in 3 America's Cup events with Luna Rossa, won a world championship with Momo 72 class, 2 European championships with French Kiss, placed 3rd in the TP52 World Championship in Scarlino. Spent 10 years with TP52 and 4 years with RC44 Artemis.

World Championship: Rolex TP52 World Championship Puerto Portals 2019

ITA|Jaro Furlani.bio: Started sailing as a kid on the Optimist and finishd 3rd at the Opti Worlds in 2000 and then 3rd at the 420 europeans in 2003. 9 time world champion on one design classes like Melges 32, Rc44, swan50 and tp 52.

World Championship: Rolex TP52 World Championship PORTO CERVO 2026

ITA|Michele Ivaldi.bio: Michele Ivaldi start sailing in Optimist then 420 and 470 before stepping in the America's Cup and big boat sailing. Sailed in the Olympic games in Savannah in 1996, 4 america´s cup campaign, winning the Louis Vuitton with Luna Rossa in 2000 and he was part of the Oracle team in the winning chalenge with the trimaran. Since 2012 sailing on RC44, TP52, Swan 50 and MAxi winning 10+ world championships.

ITA|Stefano Ciampalini.bio: Stefano Ciampalini, a skilled sailor, secured 1st place in the Melges32 World Championships from 2020 to 2022 and claimed 3rd in the 2019 Melges24 World Championship. His sailing prowess and consistent performance mark him as a formidable force in one-design racing.

ITA|Vasco Vascotto.bio: The captain of SSL Team Italy has collected in his successful career nothing less than 30 Sailing World Champion Titles, he is unbeatable in big boat, fleet racing, and makes a difference in every team he steps in: a true leader! Vasco Vascotto was born in the sailing city of Trieste, and carries with him all of the energy of the Bora, the cold wind from the Balkans that struck the bay, and all of the fire you need in order to survive the long winters there.

World Championship: Rolex TP52 World Championship PORTO CERVO 2026

JPN|Eiichiro Hamazaki.bio: Eiichirou Hamazaki is a distinguished sailing athlete hailing from Japan, known for his exceptional leadership as the captain of the SSL Gold Cup team, Rising Sun Japan. His sailing journey has been marked by outstanding achievements, including impressive results in the All Japan Yacht Match Race Championship and the Ninomiya Cup Match. Furthermore, his participation in the Sydney Olympics in the 470 class showcased his remarkable skills and dedication to the sport on the global stage.

JPN|Hideki Wakayama.bio: Hideki Wakayama, born in Hiroshima City in 1970, began his sailing journey in Hiroshima in 1996. Turning professional in 2000, he joined the Kansai-based sailing team SLED in 2003, participating in domestic races and later expanding to the east coast of the United States. Wakayama's notable achievements include winning the 2006 Farr40 Class North American Championship and becoming the Rolex TP52 World Champion in 2021. Active in the TP52 class, he secured impressive overall positions from 2014 to 2023, including a 2nd place in the 2023 12M Class World Championship.

World Championship: Rolex TP52 World Championship PORTO CERVO 2026

JPN|Norio Igei.bio: Norio Igei is a highly accomplished sailing athlete from Japan, renowned for his exceptional skills and dedication to the sport. With a remarkable track record, he has achieved the prestigious title of World Champion in the TP52 class, showcasing his prowess on the international sailing stage. His passion for sailing and commitment to excellence have made him a celebrated figure in the global sailing community.

World Championship: Rolex TP52 World Championship PORTO CERVO 2026

KOR|JIA KIM.bio:
Jjia Kim began sailing naturally by following her father, a national team sailing coach.
She started in the Optimist class and developed into an ILCA 6 class sailor, proving her skills in single-handed events by winning multiple national championship titles.
Later, she transitioned to the double-handed dinghy 470 class, gaining a wide range of sailing experience.
As a national team athlete, she has consistently challenged herself on the international stage and earned a bronze medal at the most recent Asian Games.

KOR|MINJE LEE.bio: My hometown is the beach, so I naturally like the sea, so I started sailing. I still think that the cool feeling of crossing the sea is a charm that I can't get enough of. I have won a silver medal and a gold medal in high school at the National Sports Festival, which is the most important competition in terms of major grades.

KOR|SIYOU SUNG.bio:
Seong Siyu is a South Korean sailor competing in the ILCA 7 class.
He has steadily built his race experience by consistently participating in both domestic and international competitions.
Through the SSL Asia Qualifier, he aims to take another step forward and grow further with the goal of advancing onto the world stage.

KOR|SUNGBIN SON.bio:
Sungbin Son is the pitman of SSL Team Korea.
He was introduced to sailing at a young age by his father, a high school sailing coach, and quickly developed a strong passion for the sport.

LTU|Andrius Ramonaitis.bio:
Racing for almost 19 years, Andrius Ramonaitis has experience with many classes. Starting
from single-handed and double-handed Olympic classes, he later transitioned to one designs
constructed for team sailing. He was on the first youth team in Lithuanian history to race in
AF Offshore Race and now for several years has been the skipper in „RS-280“ class, which is
one of the biggest one design fleets in Lithuania.

LTU|Emilis Valentinaitis.bio:
Emilis Valentinaitis is one of the team’s youngsters, who has been building his racing skills
for more than 10 years now. Started from 470, now he concentrates on team sailing with
various classes and already has quite substantial experience in sailing together with and even
against other team members. Strong focus and eagerness for constant improvement makes
him a great trimmer.

LTU|Gintarè Scheidt.bio: The captain of The Ambers - came into sailing almost together with the freedom and independence of her country. Growing as a high-class sailor in a newly reborn Lithuania, Gintarė Volungevičiūtė Scheidt presented her country with the highest sailing achievements so far – an Olympic silver medal in 2008, a gold at a World championship in 2012 and a huge hope and inspiration for future generations. Her positivity and sincerity are what makes the team tick.

LTU|Karolis Janulionis.bio:
A former member of Lithuanian ILCA national team and seven times Lithuanian ILCA 7 champion,
he has been successfully racing in various international ILCA 6 and ILCA 7 championships for many years now.
Parallelly, Karolis has been taking part in various ORC and one design team racing events.
Combined experience makes him a person who knows perfectly well how to synchronize
personal excellence and team responsibilities.

LTU|Klaudio Kliučinskas.bio:
Coming from a sailor’s family, he has been in the midst of sailing since three months old. For
the past few decades Klaudio has been racing in one design and ORC events as well as doing some
offshore sailing with Volvo 60 in Sydney Hobart, Fastnet Race, Rolex Middle Sea Race,
Caribbean 600 and others. His massive experience is a true treasure for our team.

LTU|Kristoforas Akromas.bio: Although he started sailing in his 20s, during the last seven years Kristoforas took part in almost all ORC World and ORC Europe events, as well as other regattas. His main strength lies not only in his team sailing skills but also in his persistence put all his efforts into enhancing the performance of the team as a whole.

LTU|Martin Volkovicki.bio: He started sailing in his teens and haven‘t missed a season for more 20 years now. Martin’s specialty is team sailing, as he has competed in such yacht classes as J70, Evento42, X-35, RC44, Platu 25, RS21, VO65. As a bowman of The Ambers team, he not only takes care of everything that takes place on the bow of the yacht but also is an example of concentration and psychological stability in most strenuous times.

LTU|Raimondas Šiugždinis.bio: European and World champion in ILCA 6 class and a keen sailor in various single handed and team sailing one designs – Raimondas Šiugždinis is considered to be one of the best Lithuanian helmsmen. His talent is supplemented by many years of experience in various ORC and one design racing events, as well as some offshore challenges with VO60 and VO65. With him by the helm, the team will fight for the win until the last second.

LTU|Rokas Milevičius.bio: From London Olympics in 2012 to The Ocean Race in 2014-15 edition with The Team Brunel and being the captain of Ambersail 2 during The Ocean Race Europe in 2021 and The Ocean Race VO65 Sprint Cup in 2023 – Rokas Milevičius has all this experience in his pocket. Knowing how to be a dedicated team player as well as a tough leader when one is needed, he is an essential personality in the Lithuanian SSL Gold Cup team.

LTU|Simonas Jeršovas.bio: Simonas Jeršovas ir the youngest team member in SSL Team Lithuania. He joined the team right before the SSL Gold Cup Finals. The athlete started his sailing career when he was 7 years old with „Optimist“ and was successfully gaining victories in national competitions and regattas. Later he sailed with „RS Feva“ „RS Aero“ and one of the most popular one design in Lithuania „RS 280“. S. Jeršovas is a universal team member and can be effective in any position.

MAS|Ahmad Faizul Aswad Mohamed.bio: An old hand of Malaysian keelboat racing, he is now a professional sailing instructor. Aswad competed in the World Match Racing Tour (WMRT) with Malaysia’s Koo Racing Team with their best ranking of 13th in the world in 2016. They came second in the 2016 WMRT USA Grand Slam Series, and has competed in the WMRT M32 series. A key crew member of Malaysia’s sole TP52 Ulumulu and formerly of Hong Kong’s Reichel/Pugh 77 Jelik, his keelboat experience lends crucial guidance to the team. He hails from Kuantan in the state of Pahang.

MAS|Ahmad Hakhimi Ahmad Shukri.bio:
Kimi is one of Malaysia’s SSL pioneers, achieving a notable 10th-place finish in Gran Canaria in 2023. He formerly competed on the World Match Racing Tour (WMRT) as the trimmer for Malaysia’s Koo Racing Team (KRT), which reached a world ranking of 13th in November 2016 (World Sailing).
A dominant figure in dinghy sailing, Kimi was national champion for eight consecutive years—first in the International 420 class (2003–2006) and then in the International 470 class (2007–2010). He has also represented Malaysia at the Asian Games and the Southeast Asian Games.
Beyond dinghies, Kimi is an active keelboat sailor, competing in the J70, SB20, and various other keelboat classes.
Kimi hails from the state of Penang.

MAS|Khairulnizam Mohd Afendy.bio: A Laser Standard sailor, Khairulnizam is a veteran of 4 Olympic Games (London, Rio, Tokyo and Paris). He is a double silver medalist in the Asian Games and a multiple gold medalist in the Southeast Asian Games. He is a regular crew member of top keelboat programs in the Asia Pacific region such as Australia's TP52 Team Hollywood and more recently Thailand's TP52 THA72. He also races in the J70, Fareast 28R and Platu 25 one-design classes in Asia. he continuosly showed a tremendous result by finishing 10th in Gran Canaria SSL World cup and will set sails for up ciming SEA games in Thailand. Nizam hails from Klang in the state of Selangor.

MAS|Mohamad Faizal Norizan.bio: Faizal won a gold medal in the Asian Games at the age of 18 and is a multiple gold medalist in the Southeast Asian Games. He has an unbeaten record in International 420 and 470 in Malaysia. Faizal and his International 420 teammate Ahmad Syukri Abdul Aziz won gold in the 16th Asian Sailing Championships in Korea in 2014 and came second in the ISAF Youth Sailing World Championships in Portugal later in the same year. More recently he has been competing in IRC keelboat regattas as well as the SB20 one-design class in Asia. Faizal hails from Klang in the state of Selangor.

MAS|Mohd Akiyuddin Mat ZakI.bio: A former national Laser Standard sailor, Akiyuddin has competed in the Youth Sailing World Championships and the Southeast Asian (SEA) Games. He currently serves in the Royal Malaysian Navy and is a senior member of its keelboat program. With the Navy, he has competed in regattas across Asia in Farr 520, DK47 and Platu 25. Akiyuddin hails from Tanah Merah in the state of Kelantan.

MAS|Mohd Azhar Sadon Zubir.bio: Wak has skippered the Malaysian Armed Forces team's Farr 520 Zuhal. He has competed in regattas across Asia in TP52, Farr 520 and DK47. He is currently head coach of the Malaysian Armed Forces Sailing Team. Wak hails from Muar in the state of Johor.

MAS|Mohd Saifullah Mohd Esa.bio: Saifullah competed in the World Match Racing Tour (WMRT) as bowman on Malaysia's Koo Racing Team (KRT). Their best ranking was 13th in the world (World Sailing Novermber 2016). Saifullah also competed in the WMRT M32 series. More recently he has been competing in the SB20 one-design class in Asia. He hails from Kuala Terengganu in the state of Terengganu.

MAS|Nur Shazrin Mohamad Latif.bio: She is a rising star in the Laser Radial class. The young Olympian has a bronze medal from the Asian Games and is a multiple gold medalist in the Southeast Asian Games. Nur Shazrin recently won a gold medal at the 2022 Asian Sailing Championships in her class. She sails for the state of Pahang.

MAS|Nuraisyah Jamil.bio: The Malaysian Ladies International 470 Champion, Nuraisyah together with her former teammate Juni Karimah Noor are the first doublehanded sailing pair from Malaysia to ever qualify for an Olympic Games. She is a silver medalist in the Asian Games and a gold medalist in the Southeast Asian Games. Nuraisyah hails from the state of Johor.

MYA|Min Min.bio: I began sailing in 2005 with the Int'l 420 Class. After completing that stage, I continued sailing in International 470 Class. Currently, I serve as the Coach at the Myanmar Yachting Federation and as the Asst. Sailing Secretary at the Yangon Sailing Club.

MYA|Min Thaw Kaung.bio: I’m Min Thaw Kaung, and sailing has been a major part of my life. I started sailing the Optimist at age nine and represented my country at the SEA Games when I was thirteen. Later, I moved into the 470 class, sailing with my teammate and gaining valuable racing experience.

MYA|Saw Thaw Thi Htoo.bio: I started sailing with the Optimist class in 2013. Following that, I sailed the International 420, the Laser, and the International 470. I competed in the SEA Games with the International 420 and also took up windsurfing. Currently, I am serving as an Assistant Coach at the Myanmar Yachting Federation.

NED|Dimitri Simmons.bio: Dimitri started sailing as a kid during the family holidays. At the age of 15 he first competed in an international event in the Europe class. While studying at the Delft University of Technology he participated in the Tour de France a la Voile in 2009 and 2010. After that he progressed into different international keelboat one design classes like the Farr 30, Melges 32, Farr 40 and RC44 sailing alongside some of the best sailors in the world and learning a lot from them along the way. On the side he also developed himself in offshore sailing by participating in the Mini Transat solo transatlantic race in 2015.

NED|Roy Heiner.bio: The captain of SSL Team Netherlands is known for making success possible. Stepping out of the comfort zone, always improving through understanding why, passionate about personal development and team collaboration, because ‘Success is not a coincidence’, it is a choice.

World Championship: The 2023 Women's Match Racing World Championships
The 2022 Barfoot & Thompson Women's Match Racing World Championship

NZL|Chris Main.bio: Started sailing in P class and won the National Championship in 1990. Then, he started professional sailing and participated in 3 America's Cup. Currently, he is semi-retired farmer from New Zealand.

World Championship: World Championship - Shenzhen Baoan Match Cup 2024
World Championship - Shenzhen Baoan Match Cup 2024
The 2024 Youth Match Racing World Championships

NZL|Leslie Egnot.bio: Leslie Egnot started sailing in Christchurch New Zealand and had an impact on sailing at a young age. She was the first female to win New Zealands prestigeous Tauranga Cup, sailed in the class unique to NZ - the P Class. At the time, it was the most competitive junior fleet in the country. Egnot progressed to the 470 class where she won a Silver medal sailing with Jan Shearer at the 1992 Olympic Games and has competed in two Americas' Cups. She is the first women to have skippered / helmed an Americas Cup yacht. She has worked for Yachting New Zealand in a variety of roles including high performance coach, logistics manager, an Olympic selector and a member of the Olympic Committee.

NZL|Nick Egnot Johnson.bio: Nick Egnot-Johnson comes from a strong dinghy sailing background, having had great success in the Optimist, Starling and 29er classes. He discovered match racing in 2018 and since then has had a long string of great achievements with his KNOTS Racing Team. He and his team are current World Match Racing Champioins (2023) and have just finished 3rd in the prestigeous Congressional Cup. He holds multiple Match Racing and Keelboat National New Zealand titles. He and his team are currently ranked the 3rd best match racing team in the world, reaching a career best of 2nd in the world. In his spare time Nick has been sailing on various boats, including the foiling moth, TP52's and Melges 40's.

World Championship: World Championship - Shenzhen Baoan Match Cup 2024
The 2026 Youth Match Racing World Championships

NZL|Robbie McCutcheon.bio: Started sailing at Wakatere Boating Club at age 7, sailing Optimists, P Class, Starling, 29er and 420. Since then he has been sailing at the highest level nationally and internationally, representing NZ on numerous occasions, Currently Robbie is sailing on the Beau Geste TP52 programboth as a sailor and shore team; competing in IRC and ORC events in Europe. Robbie is also the skipper of his match racing team competing in World Match Race Tour events in Europe and the US.

OMA|Akram Al Wahaibi.bio: He started sailing in 2007 in a catamaran Hobi16 .he joined Oman Sail in 2008 and competed in Hobi16 internationally . He used to be an Optimas coach. He Joined the Omani race team and sailed farr30, class 40, Diam 24, sb20, Figaru 3 and more.

OMA|Ali Al Balushi.bio: A member of the first ever all-Omani offshore racing team, former footballer Ali Al Balushi made the switch to sailing and has realised his dreams of representing his country. He has already tasted victory as part of the triumphant Team EFG Bank in the 2020 Sailing Arabia – The Tour, held in Oman. Ali has also been part of Oman’s successful MOD70 and M34 squads, setting records and learning from the best in the sport.

OMA|Haitham Al Wahaibi.bio: He is a professor fisherman then He started sailing in 2011 as a laser sailor. Then he become a laser coach for the Youth team. He is sailing different categories like Sb20, Farr 30 , diam 24, j70, Mod 70, maljes24 and so on.

OMA|Hussain Al Jabri.bio: Born in the coastal village of Yiti, Hussain Al Jabri’s ascent to the top has been rapid. After just one year as a sailor, he won gold at the Singapore Laser championships, quickly following this up with victory in the Laser Standard Class at the prestigious Sail the Gulf regatta. Known for his hard work, determination and intelligence, Al Jabri is ready for a new challenge in the SSL.

OMA|IBTISAM Al SALMI.bio: Oman Sail’s Ibtisam Al Salmi is one of the Middle East’s first professional female sailors. She started sailing in 2012 to become a sailing instructor and since then she has joined the national team. She competed in different boats like Laser, Farr30,diam24, J80,sp20, J70, and so on. She became the first Arab sailor to race from France to Germany and racing around Italy.

OMA|Marwa Al Khaifi.bio: She came from an athletics background. Marwa used to be a triple jumper, relay, and 100 m sprinter then she joined the sailing industry in 2014 as a sailing instructor and she is also in the Hockey National Team for women.

OMA|Raad Al Hadi.bio: In 2010, he embarked on his journey with Oman Sail as an instructor, but by 2011, he transitioned to the Extreme 40 race team as the fifth member. From 2011 to 2014, he was a key competitor with the racing team. In 2015, he simultaneously joined the Diam24, MOD70, and Class 40 racing teams, showcasing his versatility. This seasoned offshore sailor has also mastered various boats like the Laser, J70, SP20, and more. His extensive experience includes numerous victories in the Arabian Tour. Beyond the water, he's an adventurous sports enthusiast, embracing challenges beyond sailing.

PER|Augusto Nicolini.bio: Augusto is one of Peru’s best all-around sailors. After his career in youth sailing he moved on to Olympic sailing in order to complete his dream of sailing in the Olympic Games. He won a Gold medal at the Bolivarian Games in 2001 and 5 Laser National Championships in 01, 02, 04, 05, and 2010. He reached his goal in 2004 when he participated in the 2004 Olympics. He has been sailing professionally for several years on the J24, J70, Soto 40, and ORC classes. He has achieved multiple national championships in big boat racing in the previously mentioned classes. Since 2007 to this date, he has been the North Sails Manager for Peru.

PER|Christian Sas.bio: Started sailing on an Optimist at the age of 13. He then progressed through the Lightning, Laser, J/24, J/70, and larger boats. He has clinched a total of 17 national championships across Optimists, Lightnings, J/24s, and larger boats, along with a vice world title at the J/24 World Championship in 2011. He has represented Peru in various international events, including World Championships, and participated three times in the Panamerican Games in J/24, as well as two ISAF Nations Cup finals. Additionally, he has served as an Optimist coach for 8 years, both at the club and international regatta levels, leading the Peruvian Team to significant achievements. He was also a part of the SSL Team that guided Peru to qualify for the SSL Gold Cup.

PER|Eduardo Cano.bio: He has been a sailor since the age of 9, starting with Optimist. Later, he transitioned to windsurfing/J24 and surfing. At a very young age, 17 years old, he began coaching the Peruvian team for many years, which led him to migrate to Mexico to coach the Mexican Optimist team. Some years ago, he reintegrated into competitive sailing, primarily in the windsurfing and J70 classes.

PER|Ismael Muelle.bio: He started sailing at the age of 8 in the Optimist class and later in the Sunfish and Snipe classes. As a helmsman, he has participated in some world championships, several South American championships and the Pan American Games in Lima 2019. Most of his career as a sailor has been in the Snipe class, where he has been national champion twice. He is currently venturing as a crew member in the ORC class of his country.

PER|Javier Arribas Harten.bio: He started sailing optimist at 5, where he grew up in a very competitive fleet next to his captain, bowman, grinder and floater where he manage to standout in various national and international podiums. He has represented his country in almost every class sailed in Perú, achieving the title in Snipe at the “Bolivariano de Playa” as well as representing his country at the Pan-Am Games and campaigning for the Olympics’ in Nacra 17 MK2. At the moment he sails Kitefoil and ORC class as the main trimmer.

PER|Renzo Sanguineti.bio: He has sailed since he was 9 years old and never stopped. Enjoys a lot being in the sea and that drove him to keep pushing and accomplish some titles: like the South American and Bolivarian gold, and the 2nd place in Worlds Team Racing in Optimist, the South American gold, Panamerican bronze and Worlds silver in Sunfish, being ILCA 4 South American silver medallist, and now joining more serious projects in ILCA 7 and SSL.

PER|Stefano Peschiera.bio: The 28 year old and two time Olympian is the first athlete in Peru's history to win a sailing gold medal at the Panamerican Games and also the first Peruvian male sailor to qualify for the Olympic Games in the sport of Sailing (Rio 2016, Tokyo 2020, and Paris 2024). With 14 World Championship participations, he is Perus most successful and most experienced sailor. He has been ranked in the top three of the ILCA 7 World Sailing ranking. The World Cup Winner and three time ILCA 7 South American Champion is aspiring to win an ILCA 7 World Championship and an Olympic Medal.

POL|Igor Tarasiuk.bio: Born in 1997, currently representing Yacht Club Gdansk in the national sailing league and sailing champions league. Involved in many match racing campaigns as a skipper.

POL|Jakub Surowiec.bio: Started sail racing when he was 12 years old, on the optimist. since then sailed in many dinghy classes. In 2014 switched to the catamarans, and did a Nacra 17 campaign. top A cat sailor. started offshore racing in 2019 onboard vor70 class in the national project I Love Poland

POL|Mateusz Kusznierewicz.bio: Mateusz won the first ever Olympic medal in the history of Polish sailing and together he has two Olympic medals: Gold from Atlanta and Bronze from Athens. He is a four-time World Champion, European Champion in OK-Dinghy, Finn, Star and 5.5 class, as well as a podium winner in the most prestigious regattas in the world: Star Sailors League, Princess Sophia Trophy, Kieler Woche, Bacardi Cup, Palma Vela and many more

POL|Tymoteusz Bendyk.bio: Born in 1990, spend most of his sailing career on high performance catamarans and foiling boats (A-class, F18, 49er, Nacra 17, Moth). Has a Master degree in Applied physics. Lot of experience in technical part of high performance sailing.

POR|Afonso Domingos.bio: He is the first European to win the Bacardi Cup, one of the oldest and more traditional sailing events, in 2004 and again in 2008. He sailed in 3 Olympic Games, Sydney, Beijing and London in two different classes, the 49er and the Star. Has won 2 diplomas, one in each class and his best ISAF ranking was the 2nd at the 49er and the 4th on the Star. The CEO and Skipper of the best international Portuguese team, a Sailboat of the Class Soto40, the Bigamist. Nowadays Afonso keeps sailing in every kind of boats. For instance keel boats, on the class ORC to J70. On the first one he achieved the title of World Champion in 2022 and in 2021. And on the second he missed the Podium by just one point in the World Championship in this last year. He also coached many different boats, like the 49er, Sniper, keel boats... and has results such as the 3rd place on the World Championship of Snipe in 2022 and the 2nd place on the European Championship of 6M in 2022.

POR|Diogo Costa.bio: I started Sailing when I was 5 years old and at that time I was already teaming up with my Brother, Pedro Costa, at the Optimist class. In 2012, after the World Championship, I left the Optimist class and teamed up with Pedro again. We sailed in the 420 until 2016, when we were World Champions and National Champions, like in the last year, 2015. After the 420 we started on the 470. In 2017 in the European we stayed in 11th, in 2019 in the World Juniors in 4th and in 2021 we went to the Olympic Games. But since the 470 became mixed, we can't sale together anymore at an Olympic Level. So This Regatta is extremely interesting for us as we are sailing together again, for the first time after the Olympic Games.

POR|Hugo Rocha.bio:
One of the most recognized and famous Portuguese sailors, both for his passion for the sport and for his results.
Hugo Rocha competed in 3 Olympic Games. Winning a Medal in the 470 Class, in Atlanta. He still conquered 9 World Championships in the most diverse classes, from Laser II, Platu 25, J80, SB20, Swan 45 to ORC class, and he is also 5 times European Champion.
In 2023, he participated for the first time in an Oceanic race, the Ocean Race, with a 100% Portuguese crew, the Mirpuri Foundation Racing Team and after this experience he even got closer to the Ocean and improved his skills.

POR|Mariana Lobato.bio:
Mariana started Sailing at the age of seven, in Optimist Class and was born in the Capital of Portugal, Lisbon. She was representing Portugal in the Olympic Games in London, 2012 in the Match Racing class and achieved the title of World Champion in Korea in 2013!
She also sails in large boats in several teams which helped her gain a lot of experience. After being a mother of two, she achieved the victory in the Ocean Race Europe of 2021 and finished 4th in the Ocean Race of 2023, aboard of the French Team, Biotherm in the IMOCA Class. 
For her, the opportunity to learn every day with the other team members is always an asset and the Teamwork is undoubtedly the most interesting challenge on board.

World Championship: ISAF Women's Match Racing World Championship 2013

POR|Nuno Miguel Santos Barreto.bio: Nuno was born in Lisbon, is one of the sailors of the Golden Generation of the Portuguese sailing. He has a Bronze Medal in the Olympic Games in Atlanta 1996 on the 470 class and has participated in Two other Olympic Games. In the America's Cup, he was part of the Spanish Challenge of 2007 and accumulated 3 World Titles, has 5 Medals in the Europeans and 15 years of Professional Circuits always Trimming Genoas and Spis. On top of this Experience, Nuno is a good Comunicator and has a lot of Experience so it is Excellent to have him on board, especially if you want to have the boat Sailing at his Optimal Conditions.

POR|Paulo Manso.bio: Another sailor on our team who was born in the Pearl of the Atlantic... Madeira Island. Paulo Manso was involved with Nature and the Sea from a very early age. When he started to take his first steps in sailing, at just 7 years old, he immediately felt a passion for this sport. He sails until today and competes on several circuits.

POR|Pedro Costa.bio:
At the age of 6 I started sailing in the Optimist Class and at the age of 16 I started my journey on the 420, with my brother, Diogo Costa. We became National Champions of this Class, in 2015 and 2016, and in addition to many other regattas, we were also National Champions of Match Racing sub23 and World Champions 2016.
I have had this passion for sailing since a very early age and I intend to continue to follow this Sport.
Despite the fact that the Class 470 Men was eliminated from the Olympic Games, I have ambitions to participate in more Olympic Games. So I had to choose another Class, the 49er. In which I am currently as a skipper and as expected it's a big change, both personally and technically, but I'm doing my best in this New Challenge in order to pursue my dream.

POR|Tomás Pires de Lima.bio: Coming from a family of sailors, started sailing at 9. Represented Portugal in dinghy sailing, mainly in the Laser and Snipe classes. Currently competing in the Olympic stage in the Formula Kite Class. Various sailing experiences going through the Optimist, Laser, Europe, 420, Snipe, SB20, ORC, SSL47, VO65, Wingfoil.

POR|Tomás Rocha Macedo Barreto.bio:
"Tomás Barreto was born in Cascais, Lisbon, and started sailing at the age of 7, having Nuno Barreto as his inspirational uncle. Sailed in optmists, and represented Portugal in the worlds in 2014, then 420 and then 49er, where he was 3rd at the Junior Worlds in 2022.
He's cuurently the junior member of the Portuguese Team, and he's abouth to finish his degree in Industrial Engineering"

RSA|Howard Leoto.bio: Howard is a small business owner from Masiphumelele near Cape Town. He started sailing in 2004 at the Izivunguvungu school in Simon’s Town. He is currently sailing in Laser Radial and 420 class and won two national events.

RSA|Joweal Klaase.bio: Joweal is the bowman who has won the most Lipton cup regattas, the most prestigious regatta in South Africa. He is employed in a sail design office. He is also an alumnus of Izivunguvungu. He was introduced to the sport at the age of 15 by a sailing school called (Izivunguvungu) founded by Ian Ainslie and Matthew Mentz.

RSA|Marco Tobin.bio: He was born in Cape Town, South Africa, and started sailing at the age of 13. Marco actively takes part in multiple dinghy and keel boat fleets within National and International events. He`s currently the director of Zeekoevlei Sailing Centre which introduces school for transforming sailing in South Africa and is the Head of Claims Operations for Metropolitan Health.

RSA|Mark Sadler.bio: Mark grew up in Benoni, near Johannesburg. he won just about every title in south africa in dinghies and small keelboats, including a j22 worlds.he was the skipper of the south african america's cup team shosholoza. he currently lives in palma de mallorca where he forms part of the management of the north sails loft. he competes professionally on a vast array of keelboats from swan 50's to super yachts.

RSA|Michaela Robinson.bio: Michaela Robinsonwas born in 2000 and grew up in a small mining town just west of Johannesburg. She first raced as a newly born on her family's keelboat. As a junior she raced in the mirror dinghy class, crewing for her older siblings. with her brother, Ryan, she won the mirror world championships twice- once as crew and once as skipper. She first sailed the Cape-to-rio race as a 13 year old in a team consisting of her family. she then managed and skippered a university entrant in the Cape-to- Rio race, winning their division. She co-skippered a boat in the double handed mixed gender class in the european and world championships and the Nastro Rosa tour in Italy

RSA|Murray Willcocks.bio: Murray Willcocks competes in everything from hobie tiger catamarans to cape 31 keelboats. he lives in cape town.

SEY|Allan Julie.bio: My name is Allan julie. and I am from of the Seychelles. I am a passionate and dedicated sailor, currently serving as the captain of the Seychelles SSL Gold Club Team. Throughout my sporting career, I have had the honor of representing my country at seven Olympic Games, a journey that has been one of the greatest achievements of my life. Over the years, I have also won several medals at African Championships and have been recognized as Seychelles' Best Sportsman on seven occasions. These accomplishments reflect my commitment, perseverance, and love for sport. Sailing has been a major part of my life for more than 20 years. Today, I continue to enjoy the sport by racing a FarEast 28 yacht with my friends. We participate in many weekend regattas and enjoy the camaraderie and excitement that sailing brings. Beyond competitive sailing, I have a strong interest in windsurfing and canoeing, both of which allow me to stay connected to the ocean and maintain an active lifestyle. In my free time, I enjoy playing dominoes with friends at the beach near my home. The friendly competition and social atmosphere make it one of my favorite ways to relax. Looking back on my journey, I am proud of what I have achieved in sport and grateful for the opportunities I have had to represent Seychelles on the international stage. My passion for sailing remains as strong as ever, and I continue to embrace new challenges both on and off the water.

SEY|Curtis Allcorn.bio: Growing up as an expat, having lived in multiple countries, Bahrain, Botswana, St Lucia, Turks and Caicos, England, to name a few, but always periodically returning home to the Seychelles, I was always ready to settle down and truly enjoy my home islands, and after 15 years in the UAE, I did just that and bought a racing yacht.Sailing in the tropical paradise of the Seychelles, warm water and breezes, blue skies, green islands is hard to beat. I have always been enamored with the sea, a competitive sports man and an environmentalist, sailing manages to tick all the boxes for me.

SEY|Eston Dubel.bio: Hi my name eston dubel i'm seychellois sailor at the age of 13 sailing instructor windsurfing instructor now doing sail repair work sail far east 28 won manny natoinals during my younger days still enjoying a good breeze and verry happy to be in the SLL gold cup team representing sechelles.By the way i was one of first among 4 seychellois to teach sailing for the first time in my country and i'm very proud to see how far we've been thanks

SEY|Jayden Vidot.bio: I started sailing at 8 years old. From which the ocean became my playground. I do most of the water sports you can think of, sailing, surfing, windsurfing, kiting, diving and fishing. Throughout my sailing career, I’ve represented Seychelles in national and regional events in the ilca class, winning regional championships and being national champion twice. I have also done some European training events, mainly in Valencia. I have since moved on from ilca sailing and now skippering a keel boat in the fareast 28r fleet. Now currently sailing the ssl 47 boat, I’m excited to see what the future holds for my team in yacht sailing.

SEY|Joshua Allcorn.bio: Im Joshua Allcorn, a Seychellois sailor and multi sport national athlete. I’ve picked up many sports throughout my life, and I picked up sailing at 13, moving my way from Optimist to ILCA to skipper on a FarEast 28, winning national and regional championships. My life has revolved around the water and the tropics, exploring Seychelles’ reefs, islands and forests, while travelling to other countries through any sport I can compete my way into. When there’s wind, I sail/ kitesurf. Waves, I boggieboard. Clear water, I dive. Rain, I hike to find waterfalls, and of course, photograph as much of it as I can. BJJ, swimming, and sailing have taken me to many continental championships, securing multiple podiums, while creating the opportunity to explore the countru we are competing in. My goal is simple, I'm to help more people discover these sports and make our presence in international competitions much more pronounced.

SEY|Marcus Ahweng.bio: I’m quite new to sailing, I started towards the end of last year, but being surronded by so many great sailors on the team has taught me so much, so fast. I love learning new things and trying out new challenges. I think time is valuable, and learning as many new skills as possible is one of the best ways to live. A few of my favourite hobbies include surfing, fishing and free diving, as I love all things to do with water. I also enjoy photography, hiking and essentially anything to do with nature because it is a true gift. A very recent hobby of mine has been jogging and I’ve really loved training for and competing in my first marathon. But something that has really fueled me is my passion for health, whether it be health of the mind or of the body. I hope to continue sailing because it is such a beautifully composed sport and really teaches a lot: I especially love the way we humans learn to flow with nature through this athletic form of art.

SEY|Maryse Marie.bio: At first, being a sea loving kid, I started doing canoeing at a very young age because sailing was not yet introduced on the island where I come from on Praslin. In 2002, when it was introduced, I joined the classes doing mostly local competition and from then on have remained passionate about the sport and have been enjoying every moment ever Since. In 2011 I had the opportunity to sail from Mahe to Singapore to deliver a catamaran. Today, as a profession, I work as a freelance skipper, the first female skipper in the Seychelles, on board the catamaran. Doing charters around the Seychelles Islands and enjoying sailing with my guests whenever the opportunity is presented. Outside of my work, I enjoy going to the beach, travelling, appreciating and enjoying nature. Sailing now has become part of me. Looking ahead, I hope to continue sharing the experience of our beautiful islands with our international guest that come to visit the Seychelles and make them appreciate the Seychelles sailing experience. Also, to continue to encourage more women to take up sailing because there are a lot of opportunities, prospects, and enjoyment in the sport.

SEY|Roy Govinden.bio: I started sailing at the age of 11 in the Optimist class and have remained passionate about the sport ever since. Over the years, I have represented Seychelles at numerous national and regional sailing events, with one of my proudest achievements being winning Gold at the Indian Ocean Island Games. Today, I continue to compete while also serving as a part time Sailing Coach, helping to develop the next generation of Seychellois sailors. I am passionate about growing the sport in Seychelles and creating more opportunities for young athletes to succeed both locally and internationally. Outside of sailing, I enjoy fitness training, spending time in my home garden, and staying connected to nature. Looking ahead, I hope to continue contributing to the growth of sailing in Seychelles while inspiring more young people to discover the opportunities and lifelong lessons that the sport can offer.

SGP|Jen-E Tan.bio: Jen-E started sailing at the age of 7 in the Optimist class and is currently a crew in the 49er class. Having sailed single handed dinghies such as the Opti, Byte and Laser, he competed for a year in the International 420 class, before taking a break from sailing dinghies. He was introduced to keelboat racing and competed on the SB20, J24, J70, J80, FE26, FE28R, SM40s and most recently the RS21, finishing 3rd in the Summer Universiade in 2019. Jen-E started sailing the 49er class in 2018 and finished 2nd at the 2022 Asian Sailing Championships. He is currently campaigning for the Asian Games and is also working full time as a coach to fund his sailing ambitions.

SGP|Jovina Choo.bio: The captain of SSL Team Singapore has participated in some of the biggest events in sailing – and will soon add the SSL Gold Cup to her impressive resume. In a career spanning over 20 years, Jovina has finished top 3 in over 30 Optimist, 420, 470 and keelboat competitions at the national, regional and international level. Her most recent achievement was clinching the gold medal with the Singapore keelboat team at the Saemangeum Cup International Regatta in Korea. A natural-born leader, Jovina has been the captain of numerous school and national teams, and holds the key to charting the future of Singapore keelboat sailing.

SGP|Terena Lam.bio: Terena started sailing in 2011 and trained as a bowman since then. She has competed in many keelboat classes and events, including regular podium finishes at the Singapore Straits Regatta, Top of the Gulf Regatta, J24 National Champs, and RSYC Regatta. After getting into sailing competition on the Surprise yacht of the family, Eric Monnin sailed in many monohull classes, including winning the Platu 25 World Championship, as well as on the D35 catamaran fleet on Lake Geneva, twice winning the Bol d’Or.

SUI|Kilian Wagen.bio: Kilian started sailing at the age of 6 in Optimist class, then moved on to Laser 4.7, 420, and finally to the 470 class where he campaigned for the Tokyo 2020 Olympics but unfortunately did not qualify. He is currently undergoing an apprenticeship as a master sailor. He is the reigning J70 world champion.

She was able to compete at the Olympics in Rio 2016 and Tokyo 2020, where she finished 4th after an excellent win in the medal race. Today she is back in the 470 with an other team campaigning for the Olympics in Paris 2024. Maja is very passionated and dedicated to sailing, she is one of the best crews from Switzerland.

SUI|Marc Monnin.bio: Marc is a key member of the Swiss Match Race Team. As the designated Bowmen, he contributed largely to the teams climbr up the world match race rankings to finally become N1 and winning 3 European titles.

SUI|Nelson Mettraux.bio: Nelson Mettraux, 30, is a self-taught and versatile sailor. Nelson has completed and won numerous international Match Race, fleet race, catamaran and monohull foiler regattas. Today Nelson is the manager of a TF 35 and D35 Team, with which he hopes to win the Bol d'Or Mirabaud again in 2023.

SUI|Nils Theuninck.bio: U16 Laser 4.7 World Champion in 2011 in San Francisco, Nils won two other medals at the Youth Europeans in Laser Radial and Standard. He was also a member of Team Tilt at the Youth America’s Cup in 2017. Now focusing on his Olympic campaign, Nils has proven being a very competitive Finn sailor. Definitely a high potential for the swiss team.

TAH|Manutea Mahai.bio: A professional fisherman, Manutea discovered sailing in 2016. He sails alongside Teva in Diam24. He was vice-champion of France in Diam24 in 2017 and 2nd in the Tour Voile the same year.

TAH|Moana HUGONOT.bio:
A Life Dedicated to the Ocean
Moana’s maritime journey began in 1987 aboard the famous training ship La Fleur de Lampaul, a foundational experience that defined his life's path. In 1989, he entered the fishing school at Île d'Yeu, gaining his first open-ocean experience on tuna trollers. Returning to Tahiti in 1993, he initially worked as a deckhand on new longliners arriving from Concarneau, crisscrossing every corner of Polynesia (Marquises, Tuamotu, Gambier, Australes) as well as the Cook and Kiribati islands. In 1996, he completed his military service in the French Navy aboard the patrol vessel La Tapageuse, a deployment that expanded his horizons to the Tonga and Niue islands. Following these diverse experiences, his leadership led him to become a captain from 2001 to 2017, commanding various tuna vessels ranging from 15 to 25 meters.
In 2017, Moana chose to transition his career, leaving commercial longline fishing in 2019 to bring his extensive expertise to the yachting industry. Relying on his vast sea time, he officially validated his skills in 2022, earning his Master 200 and Master 200 Sail captain's certificates along with all required safety modules. As a highly qualified skipper, he has mastered a wide variety of catamarans, including various Lagoon models (620, 43, 42, 40), Fountaine-Pajot yachts (Saba 50, Isla 40, Lucia 40, Tana 47), as well as the Excess 11.
Now based in Raiatea for the past three years, where he lives aboard, he initially worked with TradeWinds, catering to a predominantly American clientele. Today, he operates as a freelance professional skipper for Tahiti Yacht Charter. Highly trusted by his clients, he is currently completing a trans-Pacific delivery from Panama. This latest catamaran project was born from a partnership with a former client and investor, alongside Teva Pichard. Together, they are also preparing to represent Tahiti in the upcoming SSL Gold Cup qualifiers in Switzerland, where Moana will serve as a trimmer.
A devoted solo father to his two children, Kealohilani and Keahi, Moana beautifully combines a unique lifetime of maritime expertise, family devotion, and an unwavering passion for the seafaring life.
