TAH|Teriimana Degage.bio: He sailed at first time in 2016, with the Holopuni. His first contest was the test event of the SSL in 2021 performing as grinder. Currently, he is a instructor in paddle canoe, the most known sport inTahiti.

TAH|Teva Plichart.bio: After racing the Hobbie Cat in Tahiti, Teva joined Match-Racing France’s Youth team. He then raced with Paolo Cian winning European Championship. In 2007, he skipped « Tahiti Tourisme » reaching Tour de France à la Voile’s 2nd place. He renewed the result 10 years later with « Trésors de Tahiti ». From 2016 until 2019, he sailed on Yliam Comptoir Immobilier winning the famous 2019 Bol d’Or in the D35 category. He continues to race with the same team on TF35.

TAH|Tom Lamotte.bio: Tom is from the same generation as Caesar. He was also his teammate in a Hobie Cat in Tahiti. Now at the Mediterranean Training Center (CEM) in La Grande Motte, he is one of the hopes of French sailing in Nacra17.

TAH|Yann Rigal.bio: Yann was on the Tour Voile 2007 adventure with Teva. His profile is versatile, with many supports to his credit: SB20, IRC, ORCC, J80 ... He regularly participates in major competitions such as Sydney Hobart or the SB20 world championships.

THA|Anusorn Ngamrit.bio: Anusorn started sailing at the age of 10 under the guidance of his father. He began with the optimist sailboat in the youth category of Thailand, JSST selected him to represent Thailand in the ASEAN Optimist Championship 2008. He then moved on to the ILCA 4.7 and was selected to participate in the ILCA 4.7 Youth World Championship 2010. As he grew older, he transitioned to the 420 and later the 470. Although he started as a helmsman, he became a crew competing in various classes in national competitions for the 470, Nacra15, Hobie16, Nacra17, F18, F20, 29er, Platu25, Fareast26, Fareast28R, Swan31, Swan42, RC44, TP52.

THA|Don Whitcraft.bio: Don started sailing at the age of 5 after his parents insisted and scared him just the right amount to keep sailing. Once he was 10, he was hooked to racing. Being in the same generation as our best Opti team ever, he learned a lot from chasing behind Nai. After taking a break to focus on his studies, he has been campaigning in the 49er with his brother Dylan. Don is super excited to get the opportunity to race against some of the best sailors ever. Besides Sailing, Don enjoys chess and exploring the world through google earth.

THA|Dylan Whitcraft.bio: With a background in the 49er and Fireballs, Dylan races competitively in the TP52, Maxi, and Cape 31 both inshore and offshore. In the rare moments that he isn't sailing, Dylan lives on a Mango farm near Khao Yai National Park, where he cycles and frequently has wild elephants as guests.

THA|Nichapa Waiwai.bio: Nay started sailing at the age of 11 after her father pushed her to try it. Although she was initially afraid to get into the sport due to social norms against having dark skin as a girl in Thailand, she overcame her fears and went sailing where she later fell in love with the sport and being on the water. Nay went on to win multiple Asian Games medals in the 29er and 49er FX which forged her reputation as a Thai force majeure. Lately, she has been competing in the mixed 470 and is also an activist for women in sports in Thailand.

THA|Nut Butmarasri.bio: When he was 10 years old, he started sailing during the holiday close to his relative's house on the eastern seaboard. Having been forced to play sports because of his addiction to computer games, he became fascinated with sailing and has been doing this sport ever since.

UKR|Andrii Klochko.bio: Andrii Klochko achieved the SB20 European Championship in 2012, followed by back-to-back SB20 World Championships in 2013 and 2015. Maintaining his winning streak, he secured another SB20 World Championship in 2016. Klochko's remarkable skill and dedication have solidified his reputation as a formidable force in competitive sailing.

UKR|Denis Osliak.bio: Denys Osliak, born on June 2, 1997, is a promising sailor whose career highlights include a 12th position in the 2018 470 World Championship in Bracciano and notable achievements in the L30 category in Marseille, France, in 2020. With a dedication to the sport and demonstrated proficiency, Osliak is emerging as a rising star in the international sailing scene, making him one to watch for future accomplishments.

UKR|Rodion Luka.bio: During his career, the captain of SSL Team Ukraine has come a long way, from youth classes to steering yachts on the Volvo Ocean Race. Among his achievements are medals from the Olympic Games and gold at the World and European Championships, in the Olympic class. In total, he climbed the world championships podium seven times in different classes of monotypes. A true leader, with experience and high performance in four Olympic Games, will certainly lead the team to the top of the SSL Nations Gold Cup.

UKR|Ruslana Taran.bio: One of the best yachtsmen in the world ever. She became a medalist three times at three Olympic Games in two yacht classes. Four-time winner of gold medals at the World Championship. ISAF ROLEX Yachtswoman of the Year. A true team player in any crew.

URU|Diego Stefani.bio: Experienced bowman and trimmer, “Scrapy” was on board in 2005 when the Memo Memulini obtained the ORC World Championship. Etchells North American champion and two times Southamerican Snipe champion, he also won the Maxi Yacht Rolex Cup in Porto Cervo in 2019 and has raced in the TP52 and GC32 classes, to mention just a few of the wide variety of yachts he has sailed professionally.

URU|Federico Caballero.bio: He sails since he has been 6 years old, when he started in the Optimist class. He then sailed in Laser, Soling and Windsurf. With a vast experience in J24, he was part of National champions crews. Sailing in Soto 40 sin 2009 as a pitman, he was two times winner of the Mitsubishi Cup, in Brazil, and two times national champion in Chile. In Soto 33 he is three times Argentinian champion, and in Soto 50 two times champion in Perú. Recently he participated in three Maxi Yacht Rolex Cup campaigns, onboard Nefertiti (Swan 90) and Moat (Swan 115).

USA|Eric Doyle.bio: Star World Champion in 1999 with Tom Olsen, Eric Doyle has been successful in different classes, but the one true love is the Star, where he often finds himself competing directly against Team USA Captain Paul Cayard. Eric was raised in Pass Christian along the Mississippi Gulf Coast, where he learned at a young age that he was hooked on sailing. Vince Brun found him after college, and he began his career at North Sails in 1992. Shortly after that he was hired by Dennis Conner to sail with Stars & Stripes America’s Cup campaign in 2000. Continuing on, he raced with BMW Oracle for the 2003 and 2007 America’s Cup campaigns. Eric’s passion is with smaller keel boats, other than the Star, like the Etchells, Melges 24, and J/70. But he doesn’t shy away from the big boats, winning the Maxi World Championship in 2004. Eric is currently based in San Diego.

USA|Paul Cayard.bio: Paul Cayard is one of the very few sailors who has competed at top level in the three disciplines of the sport: The Olympics, The America’s Cup and Offshore round the world racing. It is impossible to shrink his career to a few lines; with over forty years of experience in sailing, he more than earns his title as a legend of the sport. Cayard has won World Championships in seven different classes. He is a seven-time America's Cup competitor and circumnavigated the world twice, becoming the first American to win the Whitbread Round the World Race in 1998 and placing second with the Disney syndicate Pirates of the Caribbean in the 2005-2006 edition of the Volvo Ocean Race. Cayard is a two-time Olympian (1984, 2004), and he won the Louis Vuitton Cup in 1992 with the Italian syndicate Il Moro di Venezia, becoming one the most appreciated skippers in Italy. Cayard's accolades include induction to the US Sailing Hall of Fame (2011), and the Rolex Yachtsman of the Year Award (1998), he also serves on the Board of US Olympic Sailing. Out of all of this he will be quick to declare that his most treasured prize is winning the Star World Championship in 1988 in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

World Championship: WMRT Finals – GKSS Match Cup Sweden

USA|Victor Diaz de Leon.bio: Regarded as one of the finest professional sailors of his generation, Victor Diaz de Leon has been chosen by Captain Cayard and will represent a decisive asset for SSL Team USA, by bringing all of his experience on big boats with many crews onboard. Growing up in Puerto La Cruz, Venezuela, he started sailing at a young age on his father’s racer cruiser. At the age of seven, his father got him an Optimist and he quickly devoted all of his time and energy into the sport. After high school, Diaz de Leon moved to America, precisely at St. Mary’s College of Maryland where he was a member of the school’s sailing team. He is also a Moth expert, having finished twice in the top-10 in the World Championships.
